key_insight: Co-PiLOT solves inverse design by searching in a learned latent space, where a decoder acts as a validity prior and physics-informed optimization guides candidates toward the target microstructure.
engineering_relevance: For magnesium alloy microstructure/texture design, this provides a practical way to reduce expensive crystal plasticity simulations while still enforcing feasibility and target-driven performance.
method: ViT-based encoder compresses EBSD microstructures into a low-dimensional latent code.
Generative decoders (latent diffusion, DiT, rectified-flow) reconstruct high-fidelity candidate microstructures.
MERIDIAN performs active latent optimization with deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On an ~80,000-image EBSD dataset, ViT-FMDiT achieved the strongest reconstruction quality reported (FID 27.86) and, with MERIDIAN, achieved the best target-driven objective under a budget of 160 simulations, reducing relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: The approach depends on decoder fidelity and solver-in-the-loop simulation budget, so performance may degrade if the learned latent manifold does not faithfully cover rare but important feasible microstructures.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
